question: In major-tournament shoot-outs, how did kicks that would win the match compare with kicks that had to score to avoid defeat?
options: Kicks to win scored far more
answer: Kicks to win scored far more often: about 92% against 62%, in Jordet and Hartman's study of World Cup, European Championship and Copa América shoot-outs. Same spot, same goal, same kind of kicker; only what a miss would mean had changed. The goal was the same width; the stakes were not.
move: The same task changes odds when failure, not success, is on the line.
ask: Do I act differently when avoiding failure, rather than chasing success, is the point?
trap: Assuming a penalty is a penalty, whatever hangs on it.
reference: Jordet & Hartman, Avoidance motivation and choking under pressure in soccer penalty shootouts, Journal of Sport & Exercise Psychology, 2008
